About EdZola: Our Story, Team and Careers
Meet EdZola: a bootstrapped social enterprise in Coimbatore, part technologists and part sector practitioners, building systems for nonprofits since 2020.
Part technologists, part social-sector practitioners. Fully obsessed with building things that create impact.
The organisations doing some of the hardest work in society were still running on spreadsheets, WhatsApp threads and manual processes. <1>The intent was strong. The infrastructure was not.</1>
EdZola was founded to close that gap, and that's still the work: systems that reduce chaos, create clarity and help mission-driven teams grow.
<1>Proudly bootstrapped.</1>We have never taken external funding. We grow alongside our partners, and measure our success by the strength of the organisations we serve.
Akshay, our founder, learns how scalable software is designed and run as an engineer at Zoho.
In a government school classroom, he sees what happens when strong people are forced to work with weak systems.
In the middle of the pandemic. One of the first systems kept Mitti Café running while more than 40 of its locations were shut.
Akshay receives the Chevening Award for the work at EdZola, and we begin building towards a global social enterprise based in India.

ImpactOS: The Method Behind EdZola's Nonprofit Systems
ImpactOS is EdZola's delivery method: one way of working, reusable sector knowledge and AI tools with a person checking, so no project starts from zero.
Every project starts where <1>the last one finished.</1>

ImpactOS is the method behind everything EdZola builds: one way of working, a growing body of sector knowledge, and AI tools that always have a person checking. You don't buy it. Every system we build for you runs on it.
Most nonprofit systems are built from a blank page.
Two programmes in two cities ask the same questions about who they serve and what changed. Usually both pay to answer them from scratch. Sound familiar?
Weeks of workshops to rediscover what a beneficiary record needs, how donors move through a pipeline, or which leave rules an NGO runs on.
Quality depends on who you get
Every consultant has their own way. One build is careful, the next ships with gaps nobody checked for. You can't tell which until it's live.
What's learned walks out the door
The project ends, the consultant leaves, and everything they figured out stays in their head. The next organisation pays to learn it again.
ImpactOS exists so that doesn't happen to you, or to the next organisation after you.
Three layers. Each one moves at a different speed.
The method stays steady so the knowledge and tools on top of it can improve quickly without breaking how your project runs.
The same stages, sign-off points and named owners on every engagement, whether it's a small HR system or a year-long programme MIS.
<1>For you:</1> you always know what stage you're in, who's accountable, and what has to be true before we move on.
Everything we've learned that's worth reusing, written down once and improved on every project.
<1>For you:</1> your project starts from what's already been tested elsewhere. Workshop time goes on what makes you different.
AI and automation that do part of the work: drafting blueprints, configuring systems, cleaning data, running voice interviews, checking for security gaps.
